---
title: Basic Modelling Interface
---

This page summarizes the functions implemented in the module `Wflow/src/bmi.jl`
according to the Basic Model Interface (BMI) conventions defined by
[BasicModelInterface.jl](https://github.com/Deltares/BasicModelInterface.jl).
Wflow uses BMI as the model-coupling layer for initialization, time stepping, variable access,
and spatial metadata exchange. The implementation covers the functions that are practically required for coupled execution and
variable exchange in Wflow.

## 1. Model lifecycle functions

These are the main BMI lifecycle methods.

| Function | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `initialize(::Type{<:Model}, config_file)` | Reads the TOML configuration, determines the model type (`sbm`, `sbm_gwf`, or `sediment`), constructs the `Model`, and loads fixed forcing. This is the initialization entry point for external drivers. |
| `update(model)` | Advances the model by one time step by calling `run_timestep!(model)`. |
| `update_until(model, time)` | Runs the model forward until a target time, checking that the requested time is an integer multiple of the model timestep. |
| `finalize(model)` | Writes the final state when needed, resets the model clock, and closes open files. |

These correspond to the standard BMI phases: initialize, update, and finalize.

## 2. Model metadata and component identity

| Function | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `get_component_name(model)` | Returns the model type name as a string, e.g. `"sbm"`, `"sbm_gwf"`, or `"sediment"`. |
| `get_input_item_count(model)` | Counts the variables exposed for model input. |
| `get_output_item_count(model)` | Counts the variables exposed for model output. |

These functions tell external software which model is active and how many variables can be
exchanged.

## 3. Variable discovery and naming

| Function | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `get_input_var_names(model)` | Reads the `[API]` section of the TOML configuration and filters it to variables known through Wflow's metadata system. It also resolves layered soil names like `soil_layer_1_x` to their standard base names. |
| `get_output_var_names(model)` | Returns the same list as input in Wflow, because the implementation does not distinguish between input and output variables in the public BMI API. |

This is the step that exposes model variables by standard name so that an external coupling tool can
query them in a stable way.

## 4. Variable metadata

These functions describe the variable interface.

| Function | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `get_var_grid(model, name)` | Maps a variable name to a BMI grid ID. Wflow uses grid IDs for reservoir, drain, river, and land domains. |
| `get_var_type(model, name)` | Determines the runtime type of the variable array by inspecting the underlying pointer and returning the element type as a string. |
| `get_var_units(model, name)` | Resolves the metadata unit for the variable and returns BMI-compatible units. |
| `get_var_itemsize(model, name)` | Reports the byte size of each element in the variable's underlying array. |
| `get_var_nbytes(model, name)` | Reports the total memory size of the variable array. |
| `get_var_location(model, name)` | Returns the variable location (`node` or `edge`) by inspecting the relevant lens and routing type. |

These methods let clients discover how each variable is represented without needing to know the
internal Wflow data structures.

## 5. Time metadata

| Function | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `get_current_time(model)` | Returns the current model time in seconds relative to the model start time. |
| `get_start_time(model)` | Returns the relative start time. In Wflow, this is `0.0`. |
| `get_end_time(model)` | Returns the end time of the configured simulation period in seconds. |
| `get_time_units(model)` | Returns `"s"` for seconds. |
| `get_time_step(model)` | Returns the configured timestep in seconds. |

This is the standard BMI time interface used by forcing and coupling frameworks.

## 6. Variable get/set operations

These are the actual data exchange methods.

| Function | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `get_value(model, name, dest)` | Copies a variable's current values into a destination vector. |
| `get_value_ptr(model, name)` | Returns a view into the model's actual internal array for the requested variable. It resolves the nested model field using standard-name metadata and property lenses. |
| `get_value_at_indices(model, name, dest, inds)` | Returns the selected values at specific indices. |
| `set_value(model, name, src)` | Writes the provided vector into the internal model variable in place. |
| `set_value_at_indices(model, name, inds, src)` | Writes only the selected indices of a variable. |

This is the key BMI exchange point: variables are addressed by name, while the internal model
structure remains hidden from the coupling layer.

## 7. Grid topology and geometry

| Function | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `get_grid_type(model, grid)` | Returns the grid type. For Wflow, node-based grids are reported as `"points"` and land/edge-based grids as `"unstructured"`. |
| `get_grid_rank(model, grid)` | Returns the grid rank. Wflow uses 2D grids for the modeled domains. |
| `get_grid_x(model, grid, x)` | Returns the x-coordinates for active grid cells/node positions. |
| `get_grid_y(model, grid, y)` | Returns the y-coordinates for active grid cells/node positions. |
| `get_grid_node_count(model, grid)` | Returns the number of active nodes or cells in the grid. |
| `get_grid_size(model, grid)` | Returns the size of the active grid for BMI consumption. |
| `get_grid_edge_count(model, grid)` | Returns the count of edges for the applicable routing or land grid. |
| `get_grid_edge_nodes(model, grid, edge_nodes)` | Returns the node-pairs defining each edge, using `-999` for inactive or boundary points. |

These functions allow an external model to reconstruct the model geometry and connectivity used by the
Wflow grid.

## 8. State persistence helpers (Wflow extension)

These are not strictly part of the minimal BMI standard, but they are useful for state recovery and
coupled-model workflows.

| Function | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `load_state(model)` | Restores model state using `set_states!(model)`. |
| `save_state(model)` | Writes the end-state NetCDF output and closes the dataset. |
| `get_start_unix_time(model)` | Returns the Unix timestamp of the model start time. |

These support warm starts and external data-assimilation use cases. They are especially useful in
Wflow because the model may need to save or restore internal state between runs.

## 9. Helper functions used by the BMI layer

These helper functions make the BMI layer compatible with Wflow's nested structure.

| Function | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `soil_layer_standard_name(name)` | Maps names such as `soil_layer_3_water_table_depth` to the corresponding base variable and layer index. |
| `grid_element_type(model, lens)` | Determines if a variable belongs to a node or an edge based on the nested lens path. |
| `grid_element_type(model, var::PropertyLens)` | Default classification for node-based variables. |
| `grid_element_type(::T, var::PropertyLens)` | Special handling for local inertial routing variables (`qx`, `qy`, discharge-related quantities) that are edge-based. |

These helpers allow the BMI API to work cleanly with Wflow's nested routing and land models without
exposing their full internal structure to couplers.

This is the typical BMI adapter shape expected by coupled modeling frameworks, and it is exactly the
kind of interface needed for Wflow to participate in external or component-based model orchestration.
